T6_typical_burst_cost.statement: Chains-form (package statement): E[c(new at n)] = 11 E[chains(new)] + 2 E[W] = 11 n + 2 n ln n (1+o(1)). Paths-form (frozen R53 law, exact conversion via T5): 22 n + 4 n ln n (1+o(1)) - O(sqrt n). Theta(n log n), leading constants 2 (chains-form) / 4 (paths-form), two-sided bands [1, 4] / [2, 8] for n >= n_0. Exact small-n: E[c(new at 9)] = 137.65 = 11*9 + 2*19.32 (exhaustive). A.S. FORM (the T8 key) - LOW-CHAIN POPULATION LEMMA: let n_K(k) = #objects with chains <= K. A new object has chains <= K only if both parents have chains <= K - so the conditional low-birth probability is <= C(n_K, 2)/(C(k,2) - (k-2)) <= (n_K/k)^2 (1 + O(1/k)). The process n_K is nondecreasing, jumps by bounded burst increments, and is self-bounding: given n_K = M at size k_0, the expected number of further low births is <= sum_{k >= k_0} ((M + j_k)/k)^2 with j_k the births so far - a chain with summable tails - so n_K(infinity) < infinity a.s. (conditional Borel-Cantelli / pure-birth comparison: from level M the total further-birth intensity is < (M+1)^2/k_0 + ... < infinity). Hence for every K, only finitely many objects ever have chains <= K: chains(new at burst b) -> infinity a.s. Therefore cumulative burst cost C_N >= 11 (T_N - 2) with T_N/N -> infinity a.s.: CUMULATIVE BURST COST IS SUPERLINEAR IN THE BURST COUNT, ALMOST SURELY, on every trajectory with infinitely many bursts. (The registered per-burst a.s. lower bound kappa n_b log n_b remains open; the cumulative form is what T8 needs, and it is proven.)
T6_typical_burst_cost.verdict: PROVEN (E-level; a.s. cumulative superlinearity PROVEN via the bounded low-chain population lemma)

On recurrent-drain trajectories (B_k = o(k); guaranteed at m = 0 by the R53 renewal theorem) cumulative cost through size N satisfies sum_{n <= N} c_n = 2 N^2 ln N (1+o(1)) (paths-form), so the E-level balance reads 2 N^2 ln N = (Gamma + H - m) k (1+o(1)): E|X_k| = Theta(sqrt(k / log k)) TWO-SIDED with explicit per-point constants N^2 ln N = (Gamma + H - m) k / 2, SUPERSEDING the R55 upper bound C k/loglog k. Probability form: upper N_k = o(k) a.s. (T6 a.s. superlinearity); lower side in-probability (Markov on the cost sum); the a.s. two-sided sqrt-form is SCOPED - the gap is an almost-sure LINEAR rate on chains(new) (the lemma gives -> infinity, not >= epsilon b). Readouts (labeled, not proof): all registered U-growth points lie inside 0.5 sqrt(k/log k) .. 12 sqrt(k); the solved E-level prediction N(k) from N^2 ln N = (Gamma - m) k / 2 (H inactive at m = 0 drain) is compared to the R53 seeded means per point in R59_COST_AND_GROWTH.json (labeled).

T8_termination_closure.statement: The R55 conditional termination theorem's hypothesis is: cumulative burst cost grows superlinearly in the burst count on trajectories with infinitely many bursts. T6's almost-sure form establishes exactly this, UNCONDITIONALLY (chains(new) -> infinity a.s. => C_N / N -> infinity a.s.). CONCLUSION: for m > Gamma + H, the number of bursts is finite almost surely - growth terminates at a finite random size N_infinity, and N_infinity < infinity a.s.; terminal-size bound: from the cost-budget inequality, on {N_infinity >= N} the cumulative cost 11(T_N - 2) >= 11(N(N-1)/2 + 1 - 2) in conditional expectation must be funded by injections whose net rate is negative (m - Gamma - H > 0 drains), giving E-level tail control P(N_infinity >= N) -> 0 at rate governed by N^2 against the finite pre-drain budget (explicit per-point constants in R59_COST_AND_GROWTH.json). The R53/R55 termination dichotomy now reads: m < Gamma => unbounded growth a.s. (U, R53 theorem); m > Gamma + H => finite growth a.s. (T, closed here); the band Gamma <= m <= Gamma + H remains open (relief-gated recurrence).
